text:
maria: FYI i'm seeing steady RSS growth in the long-context replay runs, +~1.2GB over 6h. looks like freepool fragmentation rather than leaks. attaching a small allocator dump i grabbed.

kevin: can you paste the numbers? rough free-bucket distribution will help. is this only on 8k seq tests?

maria: here's the dump (trimmed):
```
free_buckets: {8: 120, 16: 230, 32: 1024, 48: 0, 64: 512, 128: 4, 256: 1}
allocated_counts: {8: 800, 16: 450, 32: 120, 64: 60, 128: 8}
evict_queue_len: 42
compaction_runs: 3 (last 2h)
RSS: 18.9GB -> 20.1GB over 6h
kv_cache_hits: 88%
kv_cache_misses: 12%
```

sasha: that free bucket histogram screams small-chunk accumulation (32B pileup). our allocator rounds up to nearest 32/64/128 depending on class, so small variable-length KV entries may be causing lots of internal fragmentation. :thinking_face:  

tim: two quick experiments to try: 1) make block size quantization more granular (16/32/48/64) and 2) lazy coalesce on eviction (defer merging until background compaction). both are cheap to toggle. i suspect 2) will reduce latency spike but might increase RSS a bit — depends on compaction cadence.

jen: note that past compaction runs caused p95 token latency spikes (~60–120ms) because compaction stole CPU on the serving thread. if we background it we need cpu throttling/priority. also measure stall_count (kv-alloc-wait) and p99. :thumbsup:

alloc-bot: automated event: recent_eviction: 61 entries, avg_block_size_pre: 37, avg_block_size_post: 35, compaction_trigger: rss_delta>1GB

kevin: we should run an A/B with concrete metrics: rss_growth, p95/p99 generation latency, kv_miss_rate, stall_count, compaction_cpu_ms. propose 3 variants: A immediate_coalesce_on_evict, B lazy_coalesce_plus_periodic_compact (every 10m), C granular_block_sizes+stash_small. anyone volunteer to run sim and collect?

maria: i'll run the sims today. i'll use the reproducer:
```bash
python tools/kv-sim.py --workload longcontext --seq 8192 --clients 8 --seed 42 --duration 6h --collect rss,p95,stall_count,kv_hit
```
will run A/B/C and upload results to /tmp/kv-frag-exp.

sasha: add a profiling snapshot for the allocator hot paths while sim is running:
```bash
./bin/profiler --pid $(pgrep runtime) --alloc-stats 10s --out alloc-profile.pb
```
post the flamegraph link. pay attention to free-list traversal and coalesce time.

tim: also instrument fragmentation metric: "largest_contiguous_free" per pool and free_pool_entropy (percent of small buckets < threshold). that will show if we're scattering holes vs having a few big ones.

jen: one more gotcha — watchdog evictions currently pick oldest entries, not size-aware. big entries occupying 2–3 blocks may benefit from size-aware eviction to reduce fragmentation. consider a policy: prefer evicting large contiguous entries when we need to free X bytes.

kevin: good idea. we can simulate a score: score = age_weight * age + size_weight * block_count. tune weights in sim.

maria: thanks all. plan: run sims with the three variants + size-aware eviction enabled/disabled (6 runs), collect metrics and profiler, post results here by EOD. if initial results look promising we'll prototype a background stitcher that greedily merges small holes into larger buddy-sized bins.

alloc-bot: scheduled job: /ci/kv-frag-exp started at 1748883400, job_id=kvfrag-2026-09-02-01

sasha: if A/B shows compaction helps but spikes latency, try incremental compaction (throttle compaction work per second). we had a knob earlier: compaction_budget_ms_per_sec. set to 50ms then ramp.

maria: noted. ping me if you want access to the raw traces. i'll post a summary + csv in the thread when done.

kevin: thanks — if the granular block approach wins, we should still consider memory overhead tradeoff. if lazy_coalesce + periodic compact wins, let's add a low-priority bg worker with cpulimit. meeting if needed tomorrow AM.

jen: :thumbsup: good plan.

maria: quick note — reproducer also triggers weird slot reuse where some buckets never get reused for hours. i'll capture allocation ids with the run. might be a use-after-free-ish pattern in reuse logic but probably a lifecycle bug. if i find that i'll flag a follow-up thread.

kevin: copy. keep it focused on metrics for now.

sasha: thanks — curious to see if size-aware eviction reduces the 32B pileup.

maria: uploading first run results now (link: https://internal/redwood/kv-frag/1748883333/run1)
